prompt:
Analyze the following system specification and identify all architectural bottlenecks, single points of failure, and security constraints:

System Overview: Sovereign AI is designed to operate on local consumer-grade edge hardware (AMD Ryzen 7 7840HS, 8-core/16-thread, 16 GB DDR5 RAM, NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4060 Laptop GPU with 8 GB VRAM). The platform guarantees absolute zero-egress data sovereignty with fail-closed security boundary policies.

Component 1: Model Gateway & Inference Runtime. Models are hosted through local llama.cpp and Ollama runtimes. Due to the strict 8 GB VRAM ceiling, concurrent loading of multiple large parameter models (e.g. Qwen 14B + DeepSeek Coder 7B) leads to CUDA out-of-memory errors or catastrophic swap thrashing. The system must enforce a single heavy model residency invariant at any time.

Component 2: RAG & Vector Engine. Vector representations are generated locally using BAAI/bge-large-en-v1.5 and stored in Qdrant. Context chunks are retrieved via hybrid dense-sparse search and reranked using a CPU-optimized lexical cross-density reranker to keep VRAM dedicated strictly to generation models.

Component 3: Agentic Reasoning Loop. A LangGraph-style state graph executes autonomous tasks with tool authorization, code execution sandboxing, and self-repair loops. High prefill costs during repeated agent steps are mitigated via deterministic prefix caching.

Component 4: Security Firewall. Every I/O payload undergoes deterministic rule-based and cryptographic inspection. Path traversal, shell injection, privilege escalation, and exfiltration attempts are blocked synchronously before reaching language models or tool executors.
Summarize the technical differences between flash attention, paged attention, and sliding window attention in the context of KV-cache memory management on 8GB VRAM GPUs.
